questions.question: Explain what trading is and name two services that traders provide to customers.
questions.expected_answer: Trading is buying goods and reselling them, usually without changing them, to make a profit. Services (any two): breaking bulk; convenience of location; stocking goods so they are available when needed; choice; storage; credit to regular customers; longer opening hours.

questions.question: A trader buys 50 packets of chips at R6 each and sells them at R10 each. Calculate the cost price of the batch, the mark-up per packet, the mark-up percentage and the gross profit if all are sold.
questions.expected_answer: Cost of batch = 50 × R6 = R300. Mark-up per packet = R10 − R6 = R4. Mark-up % = 4/6 × 100 ≈ 66,7%. Sales = 50 × R10 = R500. Gross profit = R500 − R300 = R200.

questions.question: Name three factors that limit how high a trader can set the selling price.
questions.expected_answer: Any three: competition from nearby shops and supermarkets; what customers can afford; costs that must be covered (transport, rent, electricity, waste); type of goods (perishable vs fast-moving); location.
